memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Moses said to Joshua, 'Choose some of our men and go out to fight the
Amalekites. Tomorrow I will stand on top of the hill with the staff of God in my
hands.'" - Ex 17:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joshua appears in Scripture for the first time here, and there is no
introduction. No genealogy, no explanation of who he is. He is simply handed a
task.

He will one day lead Israel into the promised land. But that is forty years
away. Today he is a man told to pick some fighters.

Great callings usually begin like this. Not with a title but with a job. David
was minding sheep. Amos was tending fig trees. The disciples were mending nets.
Faithfulness in an unnamed assignment is how God prepares people, and most of
that preparation is invisible at the time.

Notice also the division of labour. Joshua fights in the valley; Moses holds the
staff on the hill. Two very different roles, both essential, and one of them far
less visible.

Some of us are Joshuas, in the thick of the work where results are obvious.
Others are on the hill, praying, supporting, holding something up that nobody
sees. The church needs both, and Scripture refuses to rank them.

If you are on the hill today, do not despise your position. The battle below
depends on it more than anyone realises.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you in the valley or on the hill right now?
2. Are you being faithful in a task that has no title attached?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me to be faithful in whatever You have given me today, whether it is
seen or unseen. Amen.
